calls.title: GrowthBook <> MNTN - Intro
calls.summary: The team discussed the challenges they face with their current manual experimentation process, which delays results significantly. They are seeking a self-service platform that allows product managers to conduct experiments independently while providing support from the experimentation team. GrowthBook was presented as a potential solution, offering integration with BigQuery for comprehensive data analysis, alongside self-service features that unify feature flagging and experimentation. The discussion also highlighted GrowthBook’s competitive advantages, including its open-source framework and AI capabilities, particularly in enhancing experimentation workflows. Next steps include scheduling a detailed demo to assess technical feasibility with key stakeholders and reviewing pricing options.
calls.keywords: Experimentation, Feature Flagging, Data Warehouse, BigQuery, AI-powered Analytics, Platform Integration

calls.title: Growthbook <> MNTN - Demo
calls.summary: The team explored GrowthBook's strengths in integrating with data sources like BigQuery and Pendo for scalable experimentation. Key features include seamless integration for user lifecycle tracking, compatibility with existing feature flags for smooth experimentation, and namespace management to prevent overlapping experiments. The platform also offers tools for flexible experiment design and monitoring, employing advanced statistical methods for result analysis. AI-driven tools enhance data querying and insights, facilitating natural language queries and tracking overall experiment success. Lastly, the meeting addressed implementation planning, emphasizing technical scoping and a flexible trial period based on internal resources available.
calls.keywords: experimentation platform, BigQuery integration, feature flags, namespaces, monitored ramp-up, power analysis

calls.title: Growthbook <> MNTN - Trial Scoping
calls.summary: The discussion centered around the implementation of a trial to validate GrowthBook's capabilities through a low-effort historical data replay using BigQuery data. Option A was selected to minimize bandwidth and facilitate swift validation, with an emphasis on familiarizing the team with the user interface and experiment setup. Live experiments, designated as Option B, were deferred due to their complexity and resource demands. Data flow and access were clarified, establishing GrowthBook's connection to BigQuery while ensuring feature flags are managed by Harness without immediate validation. The team targeted a mid-July start for the trial, focusing on efficient preparation and collaboration through Slack and documentation for streamlined execution and governance.

calls.title: Growthbook <> MNTN - Pricing Review
calls.summary: The team is targeting a POC trial start between mid-July and early August, aiming for 30 days to validate experimentation and analysis capabilities while postponing feature flagging to streamline resources. Kirsa emphasized the importance of security team readiness, with expected minor delays due to priorities. GrowthBook's pricing model is based on a flat platform fee plus a per-seat cost, with preliminary plans for 15 standard and 5 read-only seats. Discussions included flexibility in seat allocation and trial period customization, factoring in team capacity constraints. Security considerations were prioritized, with pending information from Logan to unblock setup, and a plan to reassess trial readiness within the week.

Flexibility in contracting options was also discussed to accommodate the trial duration. Team members emphasized the importance of collaboration and support to navigate technical complexities and ensure successful onboarding.

Communication channels were opened for immediate assistance, and efforts were recognized to improve the user experience in SDK setups, aiming to streamline onboarding processes.

calls.title: Growthbook <> MNTN - Technical Check In
calls.summary: The discussion centered around enhancing security through workload identity federation while clarifying setup documentation for a scalable deployment. Edris Mohsin emphasized the preference for workload identity over static keys to ensure better security practices, with an on-premises fallback if needed. Logan Bates addressed concerns regarding the maintenance and validity of Helm charts, particularly those involving deprecated APIs, and committed to verifying the existence of an official chart. The team targeted a trial kickoff in the second week of July, aiming for about 10 users, with metrics and documentation improvements flagged as critical next steps. Communication via Slack was established for quick issue resolution, and the team will provide responses to outstanding questions before the trial commences.
